subject_session: All 15 sessions, 5 mice (sub-LA3/LA8/LA9/LA11/LA12); example figures use sub-LA11_ses-2
stated_limitation: off-diagonal cases concentrated between 8 and 16 kHz where tuning is broadest

justification.dataset: 000986 is the canonical mouse auditory-cortex pure-tone Neuropixels dataset for frequency tuning, an expert-standard choice.
justification.handling: Real LINDI-streamed data across all 15 sessions with correct spike_times_index unpacking and trial alignment, but no unit quality filtering and a slight response/baseline window-duration mismatch (55 vs 50 ms).
justification.analysis: Kruskal-Wallis, Wilcoxon, sparseness, and a Poisson B-spline GLM are all appropriate and correctly applied; the only weaknesses are the unequal-window responsiveness test and no multiple-comparison discussion, neither of which flips the result.
justification.correctness: Every reported number (1564 units, 80.5%/86.6%/74.0%, 63-100% per session, median pseudo-R2 0.024, 1157 tuned) reproduces exactly from the committed arrays, is internally consistent with the figures, and is physically possible.
justification.figures: Six clean, fully-labeled figures with units and sample sizes; the population heatmap and raster/PSTH show the effect plainly and example tuning curves display their true (including weak) pseudo-R2 values.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate and the write-up flags the 8-16 kHz GLM/raw disagreement and per-session range, but it lacks an explicit limitations statement (passive-only, no quality filtering, responsiveness-window bias), keeping it at a clean-result 3 rather than 4.
